title: Implement an Issue
bottom_line: It takes an `ai`-labeled GitHub issue, builds, reviews and tests it on a new branch, then opens a PR. Merging the PR closes the issue.

sections.heading: Run it bare for your oldest issue, or name one

blocks.caption: Every part is optional. The issue number and the model can come in either order.

blocks.title: What you can pass
rows: Your oldest open issue with the label
The model the helper runs on. One of `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`.
Looks for issues with `<name>` instead of `ai`, and gives any follow-up issues the same label.

blocks.title: Which issue it works on

nodes.label: Oldest open labeled issue you opened

blocks.caption: Without a number, it only looks at open issues with the label that you opened. If there are none, it never picks a different issue.

blocks.title: Defaults shared across the plugin
rows: Deferred work goes into GitHub issues labeled `ai`
A model word in the arguments, for example `opus`

sections.heading: You need the GitHub CLI, plus the review tools

cards.title: git and GitHub CLI
cards.text: Install `git` and `gh`, signed in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

cards.title: An issue to work on
cards.text: An open GitHub issue labeled `ai` (or your `--label` name). `/plan-tools:write-issue` creates these.

cards.title: Review skills
cards.text: The review step follows `finalize-pr`, which uses the built-in `/code-review` and `/security-review` skills, and the optional `ui-audit` and `ui-change-guard` plugins when installed.

sections.heading: A helper reads, plans if needed, builds, checks and raises the PR

steps.title: Reads the whole issue
steps.text: One helper, on the chosen model, fetches the issue and reads it in full before writing any code.

steps.title: Starts a fresh branch
steps.text: It branches from the latest version of the repository's default branch. It detects that branch's name and never assumes `main`.

steps.title: Plans first if the issue is not trivial
steps.text: Trivial means a few-line fix or a single well-scoped edit with an obvious approach. If the issue spans several files or components, needs a design or ordering decision, or the approach is unclear, a planning helper writes a step-by-step plan first, and the helper then implements that plan.

steps.title: Builds exactly what the issue asks
steps.text: No extra features, refactors or files beyond what the issue describes.

steps.title: Checks the work, then commits
steps.text: Tests and build must pass, as applicable to the repository. It commits only complete work, never partial work, with a `Closes #<number>` line in the commit message.

steps.title: Reviews, tests and opens the PR
steps.text: It follows the `finalize-pr` steps: code review, a test plan, recording leftover work as issues, then raising the PR. Merging that PR closes the issue automatically.

sections.heading: If a check fails, nothing is pushed

cards.title: No issue found
cards.text: It stops and tells you. It does not fall back to a different issue.

cards.title: A check fails
cards.text: If any verification step fails, such as tests or build, it stops and reports back without pushing or opening a PR.

sections.heading: You get a summary, the closed issue number and the PR link

after.label: After
after.text: A PR for that issue, carrying `Closes #<number>`, so merging it closes the issue.

blocks.text: The helper's summary is passed to you as it is, with no extra commentary or next steps it did not report.

also_worth_knowing: For a small, obvious issue, `/plan-tools:impl-issue-lite` does the same job without the full review and test-plan cycle.

next_action.text: Run `/plan-tools:impl-issue` to work on your oldest open `ai` issue.
next_action.detail: Add an issue number to pick a specific one, or a model name such as `opus` to change the model.
